extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, journalism educators and news organizations interested in solutions-focused reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing rigorous, evidence-based reporting about responses to social problems that explains how those responses worked (or didn't), what can be learned, and why it matters to the audience. Also describes organizational practices for spreading the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous and compelling reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions journalism is rigorous and compelling reporting about responses to social problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporting should be evidence-based and well-reported (rigorous) while also written and structured to engage readers (compelling). This opening framing underpins the other elements and signals that pieces must meet both methodological and narrative standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on a response to a social problem — and on how that response has worked, or why it hasn’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central subject of the story should be an attempted or implemented response (policy, program, intervention, innovation, etc.). Coverage should examine outcomes and causal links: did the response produce intended results, and what explains success or failure?

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows what can be learned from a response and why it matters to a newsroom’s audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond description, the story should extract lessons and implications (transferable learning) for readers and stakeholders, making clear relevance to the audience's context or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides data or qualitative results that indicate effectiveness (or a lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative data, evaluation results, or rigorous qualitative evidence to substantiate claims about effectiveness. Evidence should support conclusions and be presented transparently, including when it shows limited or no effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Places responses in context; doesn’t shy away from revealing shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain boundaries, caveats, unintended consequences, scalability issues, or contextual factors that limit the response's applicability. Honest discussion of limitations is essential to rigorous solutions coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative approach — critical and clear-eyed
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions journalism investigates and explains, in a critical and clear-eyed way, how people try to solve widely shared problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an investigative posture: probe mechanisms, examine evidence critically, and avoid uncritical promotion. Clarity of explanation about how a response works (or doesn’t) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness of responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to problems are also newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an expanded definition of news that includes responses, not only failures. Treat meaningful responses as legitimate subjects of reporting and evaluate them on journalistic criteria (impact, relevance, timeliness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Done well, solutions stories provide valuable insights that help communities with the difficult work of tackling problems and can change the tone of public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for reporting that informs problem-solving in communities and contributes to constructive public conversation. The page cites examples (homelessness, climate change, housing prices, low voter turnout) and notes research showing stories can make discourse less divisive and lead to meaningful change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network building — supporting entrepreneurial actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting entrepreneurial actors: Aligned and empowered individuals and entities rapidly bring solutions journalism to new markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of spreading the practice, prioritize enabling local or entrepreneurial actors who can adapt and implement solutions journalism in different markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network building — connecting communities of learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Connecting communities of learning: Bringing together like-minded journalism actors reinforces and accelerates learning and practice change across networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate peer learning and communities of practice so that lessons and methods diffuse across organizations and regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network building — amplifying and disseminating insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplifying and disseminating insights: Surfacing and highlighting critical intelligence speeds innovation in journalism and in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize sharing findings, best practices, and evaluated results widely to accelerate adoption and stimulate broader innovation.
